name: index-options-grid-qqq-1-har-vix-long-straddle
notes: ADR-0187 cell qqq-1: QQQ condors 1-1 calendar days to settlement, label horizon 1 sessions, chain read within 0.05 log-moneyness, 15 yearly validation folds from 2011-01-01, embargo 8 days. The har-vix rung: generated from run-real-har-vix.json (index-options-real-har-vix) by index_options.grid.grid_document, so edit the base rung or the grid table and rewrite with write_grid, never this file. Needs a pulled ./ob holding optionshist-chain (index_daily + option_chain) and cboe-index (VIX). Never decision-eligible. ADR-0197 long-straddle study: the same forecasts, chain, settlement and entry dates, but the backtest node is LongStraddleQuoteBacktest, which BUYS one put and one call at the strike nearest the entry close where both can be bought (the lower strike on a tie) and holds to settlement. Bought convexity has a negative standalone expectation in the literature (Israelov 2019; Harvey et al. 2019), except at short horizons when the VIX curve is inverted (Johnson 2017): the gate study below measures exactly that (gate_term_inverted, the closed and open splits) and the sizing study weighs it. The hedge study (python -m index_options.ledger_studies hedge) asks whether it beats a smaller condor at the same CVaR5. Generated by index_options.grid.long_straddle_document from the document described above, with only the backtest node swapped, so change the grid table or the base rung and rewrite with write_grid, never this file. Never decision-eligible. ADR-0194 entry-gate study, annotate-only, added by index_options.grid.gate_study_document to the document described above: the same forecasts, chain and trades, plus two nodes. vix3m reads the Cboe VIX3M closes and signals (index_options.nodes.VolRegimeSignals) gives every forecast row the PREVIOUS session's VIX / VIX3M ratio and its expanding percentile, the previous session's variance premium ((VIX/100)^2 less annualized realized variance) and four boolean gates: the curve inverted (ratio >= 1.0), the ratio in its own top tail (percentile >= 0.8), a non-positive premium, and any of them; an input that is missing gives null, never false. The backtest reads those rows and, per book and gate, reports the traded P&L where the gate was closed (gate true: for this long-volatility structure that is where the hypothesis TRADES, the reverse of the condor's reading), open (gate false: where it would have stood aside), or unknown: no entry is skipped, so the metrics say what trading only where the gate is true would have kept, not what a gated strategy earns. The lag is one session, so the 16:15 ET VIX close never informs a 16:00 ET entry. Needs the store to hold what the description above needs plus cboe-index-wide (VIX3M; register and backfill configs/source-cboe-index-wide.json). ADR-0196 volatility-scaled sizing study, annotate-only, added by index_options.grid.sizing_study_document to the document described above: the same forecasts, chain and trades, plus one node. sizing (index_options.nodes.VolSizingWeights) gives every forecast row three weights from the PREVIOUS session's VIX and realized vol against the expanding median of the sessions before it: size_inv_implied_var (median VIX^2 over today's, buy more contracts after low implied variance, when volatility is cheap, and fewer after high), size_inv_realized_var (the same on realized variance) and size_implied (VIX over its median, the opposite bet: buy more after high VIX), each clipped to [0.25, 4.0] and null before 252 earlier sessions or on a missing input. The backtest reads those rows and, per book and weight, reports the traded P&L as if each trade had been taken at that many contracts (total, per unit of weight, t, CVaR, drawdown): no entry is skipped and no trade changes, so the metrics say what sizing would have done, not what a sized strategy earns. The literature on volatility-managed sizing concerns equity factors and sellers of volatility, not buyers, so neither direction is presumed: hence two directions, read for a buyer. Run: python -m dskit.pipeline walkforward configs/grid/qqq-1-long-straddle.json --asof <today>.

underlying.notes: QQQ raw daily closes with each ex-date's dividend_amount (the optionshist index_daily stream, ADR-0187). since_ms is 2000-03-21 UTC midnight: the first row after the last split, because raw prices are the strike basis and the reader refuses a flagged split.

vix.notes: VIX closes, keyed by date in vix_by_date for the join.

vix_by_date.notes: dskit keyby: {date: VIX close}, the side table the join reads (one close per date; a repeated date refuses).

market.notes: Same-date VIX close as iv_index for every underlying: VXN and RVX start only in 2009-09, and the S&P 500's implied vol is the proxy scale feature (ADR-0187); the implied book prices from each underlying's own chain iv instead. A date VIX lacks keeps iv_index null.

rv.notes: HAR-style daily/weekly/monthly realized vol, backward-only. rv_22 is the reference scale; all three are inputs for a later HAR rung.

labels.notes: ln(S_t+h / S_t) over h = 1 sessions, the bucket's label horizon (the sessions its lower DTE bound spans, ADR-0187); the embargo covers its calendar reach. Rows whose horizon runs past the data keep a null label.

fwd.notes: Realized per-step vol over the same 1 sessions as the label: the target a scale rung regresses on. Every rung of a cell shares this pipeline.

model.notes: log-HAR plus log VIX (HAR-IV, Busch/Christensen/Nielsen 2011): tests whether realized-vol history adds to the implied scale.

vix3m.notes: VIX3M daily closes from the wide Cboe source (cboe-index-wide; the history starts 2007-12): the three-month VIX, the far end of the curve the gate compares the VIX to. Read only by signals.

signals.notes: Adds the term ratio, its percentile, the variance premium and the four gates to every model row, each read from the PREVIOUS session (lag_sessions 1). Every knob is written out (implied iv_index, realized rv_22, 252 periods a year, the two pre-registered thresholds, the 252-session percentile history) so this document's identity hash covers them: change one here and the hash, hence the run directory, moves.

sizing.notes: Adds the three size weights to every signals row, each read from the PREVIOUS session (lag_sessions 1) against the expanding median of the earlier sessions. Every knob is written out (implied iv_index, realized rv_22, the 252-session history, the clip) so this document's identity hash covers them: change one here and the hash, hence the run directory, moves.

score.notes: Locked A0002 scores: twCRPS on the strike zones |z| in [0.5, 2.5], Brier at the candidate strikes, PIT KS and Berkowitz. Val labels overlap (21-step horizon on daily rows), so the p-values are diagnostics, not tests.

condor.notes: Shorts at one reference SD, wings at two, a fixed 30%-of-width credit (no quotes in synthetic data). Forecast vs realized P&L is a sanity check, never a selection criterion (A0003).

chain.notes: QQQ's archived 16:00 ET quotes for this bucket only, bounded at intake (root, 0.5 strike grid, settlement-date DTE, positive underlying close, log-moneyness band); one parsed snapshot per process serves every fold. The three bounds are restated on the backtest and pinned equal by test.

backtest.notes: ADR-0197 archived-quote long-straddle backtest over val: one put and one call BOUGHT at the same strike, the listed strike nearest the entry close (within max_abs_log_moneyness) where both have a positive ask and an ask size, the lower on a tie; no quantile knob, so the model, always and implied books trade the same strike and differ only in whether they enter. The walk, expiry, settlement, American charge (short legs only), wing split, delta benchmark and annotations are the condor backtest's. The entry is a DEBIT: each bought leg at the ask, each sold leg at the bid, plus two legs of fees; the cell's credit_usd is negative and <book>_mean_credit_usd is the mean of those negative numbers. A book refuses it as nonpositive_debit when the maximum loss is not positive and, for a spread, as debit_not_below_width when the debit, fees included, reaches multiplier x the width (it cannot finish positive). The model book enters when E[P&L] under the forecast draws clears min_edge_usd, the always book every time, the implied book at the VIX-lognormal quantile and the chain's ATM iv. Fills are the end-of-day touch at zero latency, so absolute P&L is indicative. Never decision-eligible. ADR-0194: the forecast rows come from signals, and gate_fields names its four gates. Each ledger entry records the gates read from its entry row and every book reports <book>_<gate>_closed_n / _closed_mean_pnl_usd / _closed_t (gate true: where the long-volatility hypothesis TRADES), the same three _open_ (gate false: where it would have stood aside) and _unknown_n (null) over its traded cells. Annotation only: the trades are unchanged. ADR-0196: the forecast rows come from sizing, and size_fields names its three weights. Each ledger entry records the weights read from its entry row and every book reports <book>_<weight>_n / _mean_weight / _total_pnl_usd (sum of w x pnl) / _pnl_per_weight / _t / _cvar_usd / _max_drawdown_usd over its traded cells that carry a weight, and _unknown_n (null). Annotation only: the trades are unchanged.

walkforward.notes: Expanding train windows on session rows; 15 yearly validation windows from 2011-01-01 (the archive's chains begin there for QQQ). embargo_days = dte_max + 7 = 8 covers both the label's reach (1 sessions spanned at most 7 calendar days over 1999-2025, closures included) and the settlement's reach (1 days), so no train label or settlement reaches past the validation cut.
